newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Illegal workers try to flee Malaysia - report.
newsitem.headline: Illegal workers try to flee Malaysia - report.

text.p: Illegal immigrants who came to Malaysia to work are fleeing the country ahead of a December 31 deadline for deportation of those without entry permits, newspapers on Sunday quoted police and officials as saying.
Police have also stepped up patrols near Kuala Lumpur embassies to prevent the immigrants from going there to seek political asylum to avoid being sent home, the New Sunday Times newspaper said.
It quoted Perlis state immigration director Raja Yahya Aziz as saying 15 Burmese and five Bangladeshis were caught while trying to cross into Thailand. Perlis state is next to southern Thailand.
"We have reasons to believe that many more are waiting for the opportunity to leave over the next three days," Raja Yahya said.
Malaysian police, immigration and army personnel will launch a nationwide operation to catch and deport illegal immigrants from January after the amnesty period ends.
Illegal immigrants who entered Malaysia before July 31 are allowed to register during the amnesty period if they want to continue working in Malaysia.
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in October that there were 750,000 foreign workers in the country with work permits and a million more who worked illegally.
Malaysia's booming economy has created acute labour shortages and provided a magnet for foreign workers.
About 300,000 workers had been registered by 17,000 employers during the amnesty period, the New Sunday Times said.
